segments.t: Still in the communal flat, a few minutes later. Last time, the officers moved Arkady into his old room behind the wardrobe and fixed a tag to his ankle. Now Samson, the man he tricked with that humiliating kiss, is standing in the doorway, and Arkady tries to talk his way out; we'll hear it in Russian first, so don't worry about catching every word.
Самсон, послушай. Это была месть.
Месть?
Ты меня, я тебя. Теперь у нас один-один.
Ну-ну.
Всё по правилам, как рыцарский турнир.
Самсон, ну улыбнись. У нас мир.
Мир!
Ай! Мой палец!
Самсон, больше ему ничего не ломай.
Не волнуйся, не буду.
Давай руку. Вот так.
Твоя жена очень мудрая женщина. Ты её слушай.
Всё, Нинок. Теперь у нас есть личный слуга.
Что, простите?
Ты же слуга народа. А мы — народ.
Так что будешь нам служить.
Let's go through it together. Arkady speaks first, and he speaks fast.
Самсон, послушай.
'Samson, listen.' The casual command, because these two have known each other since they were boys. Then a short confession.
Это была месть.
'It was revenge.' the term for 'was',
была
, ends in an 'a' sound to match 'revenge', which is a feminine word. Samson isn't sure what he means.
Месть?
'Revenge?' the translation for 'revenge' is just one word here, and not a friendly one. Arkady explains with a neat little formula.
Ты меня, я тебя.
'You got me, I got you.' Translates literally to 'you me, I you'; the action words are missing, and you don't need them. Then the score.
Теперь у нас один-один.
'Now it's one-all.' Like a football score: the toilet when they were boys, and the kiss today. Samson isn't convinced.
Ну-ну.
'Yeah, right.' A little word,
Ну
, is said twice, slowly, and it translates to 'I don't believe a word of it'. Arkady keeps going.
Всё по правилам, как рыцарский турнир.
'All by the rules, like a knightly tournament.' He makes it sound like a fair duel between gentlemen. Then he tries charm.
Самсон, ну улыбнись.
'Samson, come on, smile.' The little word in front of the command,
ну
, softens it, literally acting like 'come on'. And then the big word of the scene.
У нас мир.
'We're at peace.' Literally, 'at us, peace'. which translates to 'peace',
мир
, translates to both 'peace' and 'the world'. Samson agrees, a little too happily.
Мир!
'Peace!' He takes Arkady's hand, shakes it, and squeezes hard.
Ай! Мой палец!
'Ow! My finger!' The finger is broken. Samson's wife Nina comes in and sees what he has done.
Самсон, больше ему ничего не ломай.
'Samson, don't break anything else of his.' After the term meaning 'not', the Russian word literally meaning 'nothing',
ничего
, stays negative too, so Russian happily uses a double negative. Samson promises.
Не волнуйся, не буду.
'Don't worry, I won't.' The second part is short for 'I won't break anything'. Nina is a nurse, and she gets to work with a bandage.
Давай руку. Вот так.
'Give me your hand that's it. That's it.' The first word,
Давай
, literally translates to 'give', and it's a very common way to start a request. Arkady takes his chance to flatter her.
Твоя жена очень мудрая женщина.
'Your wife is a very wise woman.' The describing word for 'wise',
мудрая
, has a feminine ending, to match 'woman'. Then some advice for Samson.
Ты её слушай.
'You listen to her.' But Samson has his own plans, and he tells Nina about them.
Всё, Нинок. Теперь у нас есть личный слуга.
'That's it, Ninok. Now we have our own personal servant.' Right then, Ninok is a pet name for Nina. To translate 'we have', Russians literally say 'at us there is', which is built from
у нас есть
. Arkady can't believe his ears.
Что, простите?
'I beg your pardon?' Built from the words literally meaning 'what, forgive me?',
Что, простите?
Very polite, and here very shocked. Samson explains, using a phrase politicians love.
Ты же слуга народа. А мы — народ.
'You're a servant of the people. And we are the people.' Officials like to call themselves the translation for servants of the people,
слуга народа
, and Samson takes it literally. Then the conclusion.
Так что будешь нам служить.
'So you'll serve us.' A future action word again: the expression for 'will',
будешь
, plus the action word for 'to serve'. The tables have turned on the mayor. Now let's listen to the whole scene again.
Самсон, послушай. Это была месть.
Месть?
Ты меня, я тебя. Теперь у нас один-один.
Ну-ну.
Всё по правилам, как рыцарский турнир.
Самсон, ну улыбнись. У нас мир.
Мир!
Ай! Мой палец!
Самсон, больше ему ничего не ломай.
Не волнуйся, не буду.
Давай руку. Вот так.
Твоя жена очень мудрая женщина. Ты её слушай.
Всё, Нинок. Теперь у нас есть личный слуга.
Что, простите?
Ты же слуга народа. А мы — народ.
Так что будешь нам служить.
The peace lasted exactly one handshake, and now the former mayor has a bandaged finger and a new job as the family's servant. Look after your own fingers, and that's it. See you next time!
Пока!
